techStack: React 18+ with TypeScript; all necessary hooks (useState, useCallback, useContext, createContext, useEffect, useLayoutEffect) are already imported in FavouritesContext.tsx
Functional state updater pattern (setX(prev => ...)) is already in use for the optimistic update — the same pattern is required for both the revert and pendingIds mutations
No new dependencies are needed; no imports need to change
pnpm workspace: test command is `pnpm --filter benchmark-frontend test`, build is `pnpm --filter benchmark-frontend build`
features: FavouritesContext exposes: favouriteIds (Set<string>), pendingIds (Set<string>), error (string|null), toggleFavourite, isFavourite, isPending — public interface must not change
Optimistic update for favouriteIds is already correctly implemented with a functional updater before the fetch
wasAdded is already captured synchronously before the optimistic update — correct placement for per-call revert data
pendingIds state exists and is threaded through to isPending/FavouriteButton, but setPendingIds is never called — isPending always returns false
FavouriteButton.tsx and FavouritesPage.tsx must not be modified; they already consume isPending correctly
Tests live in src/benchmark-frontend/tests/favouriteRevert.test.tsx — must not be modified and must all pass
architecture: All changes are inside the toggleFavourite useCallback body — no new functions, no new state, no interface changes
Fix structure: (1) setPendingIds add before await fetch, (2) try/catch/finally wrapping the fetch, (3) setFavouriteIds functional revert inside catch
The useCallback dependency array [favouriteIds] is unchanged — wasAdded already closes over favouriteIds correctly
localStorage sync (useEffect on favouriteIds) is unaffected — it runs after any setFavouriteIds call including the revert
edgeCases: Concurrent toggle on a different product while product A is in-flight: functional updater reads from prev (latest state), so product B's toggle is not clobbered when product A reverts — covered by using setFavouriteIds(prev => ...) not a stale Set literal
Concurrent toggle on same product: each call captures its own wasAdded and reverts its own change independently; button disabled via isPending reduces likelihood but is not the only guard
Fetch rejects after another successful toggle on the same product in a prior call: wasAdded is per-call-scoped, so the revert direction is always correct for this specific call
Success path: catch block does not run, optimistic state is preserved; finally still runs and cleans up pendingIds
Failure path: catch reverts favouriteIds, then finally runs and cleans up pendingIds — ordering is correct
setPendingIds add must appear before await fetch (not after) so isPending returns true during the entire request lifetime

tasks.requirement: Requirements 3 & 4 — setPendingIds must add productId before fetch and remove it in a finally block
tasks.description: In toggleFavourite, add `setPendingIds(prev => { const next = new Set(prev); next.add(productId); return next; })` immediately before the try block (or at the start of the try, before await fetch). Wrap the existing try/catch in a try/catch/finally and add `setPendingIds(prev => { const next = new Set(prev); next.delete(productId); return next; })` inside the finally block.

tasks.requirement: Requirements 1 & 2 — catch block must revert the optimistic update using a functional state updater that reads wasAdded
tasks.description: In the catch block of toggleFavourite, add `setFavouriteIds(prev => { const next = new Set(prev); if (wasAdded) next.delete(productId); else next.add(productId); return next; })` before the existing setError call. The updater must take a callback (not a Set literal) so concurrent toggles on other products are not clobbered.
